## objective
own auth build (spec review waived by the human): Supabase Auth, own Account screen, withSession, Settings account section
- discovery: Human decision 2026-10-10 15:45: "we dont need to use clerk it might be better to have our own auth ... also because of our design". Clerk is dropped (never installed on goal/T-0001). Auth is Supabase Auth on the existing project (ref hrwhjngmrdoxkxgnlrra), with sign-in screens we draw ourselves in the app's design. Work in your own worktree from goal/T-0001 (head fb2f47c). Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first; add the one new dependency with `pnpm add @supabase/supabase-js` (pnpm-lock.yaml stays the only lockfile). No Clerk package, no other new dependency.

Design rule: the app stays fully usable signed out and offline; an account only adds sync. Only VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY are client-side. Never log a password, token or session. The database already keys every row on `auth.jwt()->>'sub'` (supabase/migrations/20261010120000_init.sql, applied live), which Supabase Auth fills with the user id, so NO migration change.

Read first: src/App.tsx, src/main.tsx, src/screens/Settings.tsx (keep the T-0034 glass styling and the T-0037 Gemma licence line untouched), src/screens/Settings.test.tsx, src/test/setup.ts, src/sync/schema.ts, src/styles or tokens file used by T-0034, docs/SUPABASE.md, .env.example, README.md.

1. src/sync/supabase.ts
   - `getSupabase()` returns ONE memoised supabase-js client from VITE_SUPABASE_URL + VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY with auth options {persistSession: true, autoRefreshToken: true, detectSessionInUrl: false, storageKey: "alltag.auth"} (localStorage works in the Capacitor webview); null when either var is missing.
   - `isSupabaseConfigured()`.
   - `withSession<T>(fn: (client, userId: string) => Promise<T>): Promise<T | null>`: returns null WITHOUT calling fn unless configured AND `client.auth.getSession()` yields a session; otherwise calls fn with the client and session.user.id. This is the only door for the sync task: signed out means no network at all.
   - `__resetSupabaseForTests()`.
2. src/auth/auth.tsx
   - Context default DISABLED = {status: "disabled", userId: null, address: null, signIn, signUp, signOut, resetError, error: null} where the functions resolve to {ok: false, error: "off"}.
   - `AuthProvider`: not configured -> provides DISABLED, no network. Configured -> status "loading" until the first `getSession()` resolves, then "signed_in" (userId = user.id, address = user.email) or "signed_out"; subscribes to `onAuthStateChange` and unsubscribes on unmount.
   - `signIn(address, password)` -> supabase.auth.signInWithPassword; `signUp(address, password)` -> supabase.auth.signUp; returns {ok, needsConfirm, error}. needsConfirm = true when signUp returns a user but no session (project requires confirming the address). `signOut()` -> supabase.auth.signOut(). Map errors to calm copy: invalid credentials -> "that address and password don't match"; user exists -> "there is already an account for this address, sign in instead"; weak password -> "use at least 8 characters"; network/fetch -> "no connection, try again when you are online"; anything else -> "something went wrong, try again".
   - `useAuth()` reads only the context.
   - main.tsx wraps <App/> in <AuthProvider>.
3. src/screens/Account.tsx (our own sign-in UI, no third-party widgets): a sheet/screen in the T-0034 design language (paper ground, large title, glass close button, moss primary capsule, calm lowercase copy). Two modes switched by a segmented control: "sign in" and "create account". Fields: address (<label>, type email, autocomplete email/username) and password (<label>, type password, autocomplete current-password or new-password), a show/hide password toggle button with aria-label. Client validation before calling: address must contain "@" and a dot after it, password at least 8 characters; inline error line under the fields (role="alert"). Primary button text "sign in" / "create account", disabled while pending with a spinner. Below: "not now" text button that closes. Footnote: "optional. without an account everything stays on this phone. your words sync to an EU server (Supabase)." After needsConfirm: replace the form with "check your inbox to confirm your address, then sign in here." and a "back to sign in" button. On success: close and return to Settings.
   - Reachable from Settings (and from onboarding's "I have an account" link if onboarding has one; if not, skip). Use whatever routing/overlay pattern App.tsx already uses for screens.
4. Settings: an "account" section above the offline tutor section. disabled -> muted "sync is off in this build". loading -> muted "checking your account…". signed_out -> "sign in to sync your words, scenes and conversations across devices. everything also works without an account." + primary moss capsule "sign in" opening Account. signed_in -> the address, "signed in", a "sync" row reading "ready" (U3 fills it), secondary "sign out".
5. Docs and config: docs/SUPABASE.md replaces every Clerk mention with a Supabase Auth section (email + password, the "Confirm email" project setting and what the app does in each case, no redirect URLs needed because there are no magic links, sessions stored on the device under alltag.auth, sign-out keeps local data). .env.example: delete the Clerk line; the anon key comment says "RLS on auth.jwt() sub protects the data". README env list: drop Clerk. supabase/config.toml: if it has an [auth] section, set `site_url` unchanged and add `[auth.email] enable_signup = true` only if absent (do not change other keys).
6. Tests (mock @supabase/supabase-js createClient locally per file with vi.hoisted spies; no global mocks in src/test/setup.ts):
   - src/sync/supabase.test.ts: null when unconfigured; one client; withSession does not call fn without a session; calls fn with userId when a session exists.
   - src/auth/auth.test.tsx: no env -> disabled and createClient never called; configured -> loading, then signed_in after getSession; onAuthStateChange sign-out flips to signed_out; unsubscribe on unmount; signIn/signUp map the five error cases; needsConfirm when signUp returns no session.
   - src/screens/Account.test.tsx: validation blocks bad address and short password without calling signIn; signIn called with the typed values; error line renders the mapped copy; create-account with needsConfirm shows the confirm message; "not now" closes.
   - Settings.test.tsx: the four account states by wrapping in the auth context with test values; existing Settings tests stay green unchanged (they render outside AuthProvider and get DISABLED).
Finish: `npm test -- --watch=false`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `pnpm build`. `git grep -n -i clerk -- src docs .env.example README.md` must find nothing. Commit as "U2 v4: own auth with Supabase Auth (password), our own sign-in screen, withSession for sync" and report `git diff --name-only HEAD~1`.

# Supabase and Supabase Auth

The app works fully signed out and offline. Local storage is the source of truth on the device. An account only adds sync: signed in, the app pushes and pulls rows and scene photos to Supabase.

## How the pieces fit

- **Supabase Auth is the identity provider.** The app signs in with email and password through supabase-js, on screens we draw ourselves (`src/screens/Account.tsx`). No third-party widget.
- **RLS keys everything on the JWT sub.** `public.current_user_id()` returns `auth.jwt()->>'sub'`, which Supabase Auth fills with the user id (a uuid). Every table has `user_id text` defaulting to it, and one policy per operation allows only `user_id = public.current_user_id()`. The anon role has no access.
- **Storage.** Private bucket `scenes`. Path convention: `<sub>/<sceneId>.jpg`. Storage policies allow a user only objects whose first folder is their sub. `scenes.image_path` stores that path.
- **Sync columns.** Every table has `updated_at` (set by the `set_updated_at` trigger) and `deleted_at` (soft delete), indexed on `(user_id, updated_at)` so a pull is "my rows changed since t".

| table | key | what |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `profiles` | `user_id` | level (A1 to B2), display name, settings |
| `items` | `id` uuid | kept phrases and SM-2 state in `srs` (interval, ease, reps, due) |
| `scenes` | `id` uuid | captured place, objects, task, photo path |
| `conversations` | `id` uuid | roleplay transcript lines, duration, kept count |

Row types for the client: `src/sync/schema.ts` (`ProfileRow`, `ItemRow`, `SceneRow`, `ConversationRow`, `TABLES`, `BUCKET`). The SQL is `supabase/migrations/20261010120000_init.sql`.

## Supabase Auth

- **Email and password only.** Sign in calls `signInWithPassword`, create account calls `signUp`. There are no magic links and no OAuth, so no redirect URLs need to be configured.
- **Password length.** The project setting Authentication > Providers > Email > minimum password length is the server-side floor (Supabase default 6). The app enforces at least 8 characters before it calls Supabase.
- **"Confirm email" setting.** Off on the live project (`enable_confirmations = false` in `supabase/config.toml`).
  - Off: `signUp` returns a session and the user is signed in at once. A second sign-up with the same address answers `user_already_exists`; the app says "there is already an account for this address. sign in instead." and switches to sign in.
  - On: `signUp` returns a user but no session. The app shows "check your inbox to confirm your address, then sign in here." with a way back to sign in. An existing address then comes back as a user with no identities; the app shows the same neutral line so nobody learns which addresses exist.
- **Sessions stay on the device** in localStorage under the key `alltag.auth` (works in the Capacitor webview). supabase-js refreshes the token on its own.
- **Sign out keeps local data.** Only the session is removed; words, scenes and conversations stay on the phone.
- **Sync goes through `withSession`** in `src/sync/supabase.ts`. Signed out, it returns null and makes no network call.

## Keys

Only public values go to the client, as `VITE_*` vars: the Supabase project URL and anon key. No service role key is used or stored anywhere in the repo.

## One-time setup (human)

The hosted project is `alltag` in region eu-central-2 (Zurich).

1. **Supabase dashboard**
   - Authentication > Providers > Email: enabled, "Confirm email" off, minimum password length at least 6 (the app asks for 8).
   - Or from the CLI: `supabase config push` (reads `supabase/config.toml`).
2. **Schema**
   - `supabase link --project-ref <ref>`
   - `pnpm db:push` (runs `supabase db push`). This creates the tables, policies and the `scenes` bucket.
   - Optional: `pnpm db:types` writes generated types to `src/sync/database.types.ts`.
3. **Env vars**, in `.env` locally and in the Vercel project settings:
   - `VITE_SUPABASE_URL`: Project Settings > API > Project URL.
   - `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`: Project Settings > API > anon public key.

Without these vars the app runs local-only and Settings says "sync is off in this build".

**Summary**
- `src/sync/supabase.ts`: one shared client, built only when the two Supabase env vars are set (read at call time). `withSession` returns null with no network call when signed out or unconfigured, if reading the session fails, or if refreshing an expiring session fails. Errors from `fn` pass through unchanged.
- `src/auth/auth.tsx`: sign-in status comes only from Supabase's auth events. If no event arrives within 4 s, it reads the stored session once with its own 3 s timeout, and offline that ends as signed out. Errors are mapped to calm copy by code first, then the offline check, then a generic line. The provider owns the Account overlay through `openAccount()` and `closeAccount()`.
- `src/screens/Account.tsx` is our own sign-in screen in the existing glass design. Settings has the new account section above the offline tutor. `main.tsx` wraps the app in the provider; `App.tsx` is unchanged.
- Docs and config: SUPABASE.md, `.env.example`, README and `supabase/config.toml` have the Clerk parts removed and the email sign-in settings added. Comments fixed in `schema.ts` and `seed.sql`. The applied migration and `migrations.test.ts` are untouched.

1. The mock spreads the real `@supabase/supabase-js`, so `isAuthRetryableFetchError` stays real.
2. `AuthContext` is exported so Settings and Account tests can supply test values.

5. The README names the three `VITE_` vars: `VITE_API_BASE`, `VITE_SUPABASE_URL`, `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`.

**Two things I added beyond the spec:**
- `AuthResult` has an extra `existing` flag. Account uses it to switch to sign in when an address already has an account.
